title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters
blurb: Zero to One grew out of a class on startups that Peter Thiel taught at Stanford, with notes shaped by his student Blake Masters. Its central claim is that real progress comes from creating new things, going from zero to one, rather than copying what already exists. Thiel challenges common business wisdom. He argues that competition destroys profits, and that great companies aim to become monopolies by owning a small market and then expanding. He urges founders to hunt for important truths that others overlook. He also asks them to treat the future as something you can plan and shape, not leave to chance. Drawing on his experience co-founding PayPal and investing early in Facebook, he explains why a few winners dominate outcomes, and why every business should be able to answer seven hard questions.

lessons.b: Real progress comes from creating something new, which is vertical progress, rather than copying what already works, which is horizontal progress.
Great businesses start by asking what important truth very few people agree with you on, because every new company is built on a hidden secret.
